notes: Of the three statute records a round-55 agent returned, Bahrain and Cambodia are filed as written. OMAN WAS REWRITTEN: the agent's record rested on the Banking Law of Royal Decree 114/2000, which it flagged might have been superseded, and it has been. Royal Decree 2/2025 took effect on 1 January 2025 and its Article IV expressly repeals Royal Decree 114/2000, so filing those articles as a standing arrangement with no end date would have stated something false on the map. The replacement rests on the current framework instead, which carries the same finding: Royal Decree 4/2025 seats the Minister of Economy as Deputy Chairman of the board and the Undersecretary of the Ministry of Finance as a member, and Royal Decree 5/2025 appoints the Governor with the rank of Minister. BRUNEI was added, which the agent found but did not file because it never obtained the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank Order 2010 itself. The bank's own announcement of 21 October 2025 names a board chaired by a serving minister and deputy-chaired by a deputy minister, which is the Laos shape documented by the bank rather than by the statute, and the record says so on its face. Qatar, Tajikistan and Macao stay unsettled; the reasons are in this round's research log.

records.summary: Bahrain's Central Bank of Bahrain and Financial Institutions Law, promulgated by Law No. (64) of 2006 of 6 September 2006 and in force the day after publication, keeps the executive over the bank by its own terms: Article 5 puts all seven members of the Board of Directors, one of them a representative of the Ministry of Finance, in office by Royal Decree for renewable four-year terms, and the appointing Decree names the Chairman and Vice Chairman; Article 10 appoints the Governor, who is of ministerial rank, by Royal Decree for a renewable five-year term; and Article 173 has the Minister monitor the bank's adherence to 'the general economic policy of the Kingdom' and, where the Minister finds a conflict and the Board insists on its opinion, refer that conflict to the Cabinet, which resolves it by an order issued within thirty days. This is a standing statutory arrangement with no end date and no episode attached to it.
records.source_title: Law No. (64) of 2006 with respect to promulgating the Central Bank of Bahrain and Financial Institutions Law (consolidated English text, Legislation & Legal Opinion Commission, Kingdom of Bahrain)

records.summary: Cambodia's Law on the Organization and Conduct of the National Bank of Cambodia, promulgated on 26 January 1996, gives the executive the bank's leadership and part of its currency power: Article 13 provides that the Governor and the Deputy Governor are 'appointed, replaced and dismissed by a royal decree on the recommendation of the Royal Government', stating in that article no grounds that must be met for a dismissal, while a separate Article 14 lists reasons a Board member must cease office, including conviction of a criminal or administrative offence, without saying whether those reasons govern the Governor and Deputy Governor; the other Board members are appointed, replaced and dismissed by sub-decree; Article 12(1) seats on the seven-member Board both a representative of the Ministry of Economy and Finance and a representative of the head of the Royal Government; and Article 45 bars the bank from withdrawing or calling in currency without the Royal Government's consent. Policy itself is set by the Board, which Articles 7(1) and 29 require only to consult the Royal Government. This is a standing statutory arrangement with no end date and no episode attached to it.
records.source_title: Law on the Organization and Conduct of the National Bank of Cambodia (English text, National Committee for Sub-National Democratic Development library, Royal Government of Cambodia)

records.summary: Oman rebuilt the legal framework around its central bank with effect from 1 January 2025, and the executive sits inside the bank under it. Royal Decree 2/2025 issued a new Banking Law repealing the Banking Law of Royal Decree 114/2000, and Royal Decree 3/2025 issued the System of the Central Bank of Oman, a twenty-one article statute that operates as the bank's own governing act and is described as granting it legal, financial and administrative independence. The Board is then constituted by decree rather than by the bank: Royal Decree 4/2025 appointed HH Sayyid Taimour bin Asaad bin Tarik al Said as Chairman of the Board of Directors and made the Minister of Economy its Deputy Chairman, with the Governor of the Central Bank, the Undersecretary of the Ministry of Finance and the Chairman of the Financial Services Authority among the members, and Royal Decree 5/2025 appointed Ahmed bin Jaafar bin Salim al Musallami as Governor with the rank of Minister. This is a standing arrangement with no end date and no episode attached to it.
records.source_title: His Majesty issues 9 decrees, ratifies state budget (Oman Observer), setting out Royal Decrees 2/2025, 3/2025, 4/2025 and 5/2025

records.kind: government ministers chair and sit on the central bank's board
records.summary: Brunei Darussalam Central Bank announced on 21 October 2025 that His Majesty the Sultan had consented to the appointment of its Board of Directors, and the board it lists is made of serving government officers. The Chairman is the Minister of Primary Resources and Tourism and the Deputy Chairman is the Deputy Minister of Finance and Economy (Fiscal); the other members are the Deputy State Mufti, the Permanent Secretary (Wawasan) of the Prime Minister's Office, the Permanent Secretary (Economy, Trade and Industry) of the Ministry of Finance and Economy, the Solicitor General, and the bank's own Managing Director. The announcement gives no term. This record rests on the bank's own published announcement of who sits on its board rather than on the text of the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank Order 2010, which the bank does not publish in any crawlable index and which could not be obtained.
records.source_title: Appointment of BDCB Board of Directors, announcement reference BDCB/COMMS/3, 21 October 2025
